parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Start with work, then design roles
parts.body:
An AI talent plan begins with the funded portfolio and the work needed to deliver it. Inventory product discovery, domain judgment, data stewardship, software and platform engineering, evaluation, security, privacy, procurement, and change management. Mark which capabilities already exist, how much capacity they have, and where a single person is carrying an unsafe number of duties. A list of fashionable job titles does not reveal whether the first two pilots can be evaluated and operated.

Map tasks to decisions. An AI product lead owns workflow fit and outcome measurement. Engineers own integration and service reliability. Evaluators design representative cases and investigate errors with domain experts. Data stewards own data quality and access processes; security and privacy specialists apply their established controls. A model specialist is necessary when the portfolio requires such expertise, but a company using managed services may need evaluation and integration first. People can cover several tasks in a small organization if review independence and capacity remain credible.

The OECD's research on firms reports skills and management understanding as barriers to adoption. Treat hiring, training, partner support, and reuse as possible remedies. The choice should answer a documented gap with an owner, workload estimate, and six-month result.

example.title: A useful gap
example.body: A firm has two domain experts and platform engineers, but neither team can grade whether a generated answer cites the right contract clause. Hiring another model engineer will not close that gap. It can train domain reviewers, appoint an evaluation lead, and reserve reviewer capacity before the pilot.

exercise.title: Make a capability map
exercise.body: List the tasks required for your next two AI uses from discovery to incident response. For each, record current owner, capacity, evidence of competence, gap, and whether to train, hire, borrow, or outsource. Flag any duty with no named owner.

sources: OECD: adoption of AI in firms
NIST AI RMF Core: roles and multidisciplinary perspectives

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Sequence hires under a real constraint
parts.body:
Suppose two pilots and one shared platform have funding, but only three hires are approved. Rank the bottlenecks that could prevent a safe result in the next six months. If the organization already has strong engineering, an AI product leader, evaluation lead, and change or data specialist may be more useful than three model developers. If there is no dependable infrastructure, a platform engineer moves up the list. State what work existing staff and partners will perform in each case.

Write a role charter for each hire: the decisions the person owns, deliverables, interfaces, and what success looks like after six months. 'AI strategy' alone is too vague. A product lead could be measured on a validated workflow baseline and a pilot decision packet. An evaluation lead could deliver a representative dataset, grading protocol, error analysis, and production sampling plan. Avoid measuring staff solely by prompt count or number of demos.

Check dependencies before opening requisitions. A specialist who starts after a pilot launches cannot establish its pre-launch baseline. A reviewer with no allocated time cannot approve a controlled release. Budget for training and backfill as well as new salaries.

example.title: A six-month capacity and cost table
example.body: Illustrative organization: two customer-facing pilots, mature platform engineering, and a $200,000 six-month talent cap. Capacity and fully loaded six-month costs: evaluation lead, 1.0 FTE, $90,000; domain reviewer, 0.5 FTE redeployed, $45,000; backfill for that reviewer's former duties, $18,000; training time for two existing product managers, $12,000; specialist partner for the first evaluation protocol and coaching, $30,000. Total $195,000, leaving $5,000 contingency. The manager assigns one product manager to each pilot; existing engineers, data stewards, security, and privacy staff retain their duties, with their incremental project time separately budgeted in the pilots. Recruit the evaluation lead before live testing, contract the partner for weeks 1–8 while hiring, and start reviewer calibration in month 1. By month 3, the lead and two internal reviewers must independently reproduce the protocol on 100 seeded cases and agree on at least 90% of grades; investigate every material disagreement. The 90% is an illustrative transfer criterion, not a general benchmark. If pilot two is cancelled at the month 3 gate, reassign its product manager and reviewer allocation to the surviving use rather than adding another specialist. Hire a model engineer only if evaluated cases reveal a customization need that current staff and vendor support cannot meet.

exercise.title: Defend the first three roles
exercise.body: Choose three roles under a hiring cap. Give each the first deliverable, decision right, dependency on current staff, six-month evidence of success, and a risk if the hire is delayed. Explain one attractive role you would defer and what signal would reverse that decision.

sources: OECD: bridging the AI skills gap

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Build capability inside existing teams
parts.body:
Training works when staff use a skill in their own workflow and receive feedback. Give product managers practice writing a value hypothesis and release criteria. Give domain reviewers difficult cases to grade consistently. Teach engineers to capture versions, logs, and fallbacks. Teach managers how to inspect corrections and capacity changes. A common introduction to AI is useful, but these groups need different practice. The OECD's skills research distinguishes specialist demand from wider workforce learning.

Pair external specialists with internal counterparts and require reusable artifacts: evaluation sets, runbooks, decision logs, and annotated failure examples. A vendor can accelerate a pilot, but the company must still own its use-case decision and understand how to operate or stop the system. Set a transfer milestone before a partner's contract ends. Review whether staff can repeat a task without that partner, rather than counting completed training sessions.

Protect the time. If domain experts are expected to evaluate outputs on top of a full workload, quality checks become rushed. Put review hours into the business case and backfill critical duties. Track retention risk where only one specialist understands an essential system.

example.title: A partner exit test
example.body: A partner builds the first grading guide with domain experts. Before the contract ends in week 8, two employees separately grade 100 representative and seeded failure cases without the partner, reconcile material differences, rerun the evaluation after a model change, and produce a release recommendation that names unresolved risk. The partner may leave only after the evaluation lead signs the artifacts and the employees can repeat the process. The sample and criterion are illustrative; the organization sets them for its risk.

exercise.title: Design a six-week learning plan
exercise.body: Choose one existing role. Give it a real task, a coach, time allocation, graded artifact, and follow-up check in six weeks. Specify how you will know the person can perform the task without the coach.

sources: OECD: bridging the AI skills gap
NIST AI RMF Core: organizational competency and roles

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Present a talent investment case
parts.body:
A board or CEO needs to see the capability bottleneck, not a headcount wish list. Describe the portfolio's expected workload, existing capacity, hires or training proposed, cost including backfill, and the decisions that become possible. Separate permanent capability from a temporary surge. A contractor may fill a time-bound integration gap; an enduring evaluation function needs internal ownership even if outside experts help build it.

Show a sequence with review points. Fund an evaluation lead now if the next release lacks representative tests; delay a second product lead until the first two pilots prove demand. State how a role will be assessed and what project risk remains while it is vacant. This makes the personnel request falsifiable.

For a multinational organization, include domain and language capacity in the relevant markets. A central English-language testing team cannot assume its results transfer to French services in Canada or local EU workflows. Coordinate with local employees and control owners when evaluating consequential uses. Treat regional expertise as part of delivery, not a courtesy review at the end.

example.title: A capped talent decision packet
example.body: Approve up to $200,000 for six months, against the $195,000 allocation above. Month 2 gate: hire or interim lead in place and first evaluation protocol tested; otherwise pause the first release. Month 3 gate: internal team passes the unassisted transfer test and pilot two remains funded; otherwise return its capacity to pilot one and review the partner contract. Month 6 gate: two documented evaluation protocols, an owned production sampling plan, and a measured release decision. Finance checks loaded costs and the $5,000 reserve before any extra commitment. These are example terms, not a standard staffing ratio.

exercise.title: Write the CEO note
exercise.body: In 200 words, justify three roles or training allocations against two funded uses. Include six-month deliverables, total capacity cost, a make-or-buy choice, a succession risk, and one condition for revisiting the plan.

sources: OECD: adoption of AI in firms
